headword: {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}
reading: しゅうしょくかつどう

definitions.explanation: The process of seeking employment, especially the structured job-hunting season undertaken by university students in Japan. Often abbreviated to 就活 (しゅうかつ).

examples.japanese: {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}が{始|はじ}まった。
{大学|だいがく}3{年生|ねんせい}から{就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}を{始|はじ}める{学生|がくせい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many students start job hunting from their third year of university.

examples.japanese: {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}では、{面接|めんせつ}の{練習|れんしゅう}だけでなく、{自己分析|じこぶんせき}も{重要|じゅうよう}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: In job hunting, it is said that self-analysis is just as important as practicing for interviews.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
In Japan, {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう} refers to the highly structured job-search process that university students go through, typically starting in their third year. It involves attending company information sessions, submitting entry sheets, and going through multiple rounds of interviews.

ABBREVIATION:
Almost always shortened to {就活|しゅうかつ} in casual speech and even in news reports. The full form {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう} appears in formal or written contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}を{始|はじ}める (start job hunting)
- {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}に{励|はげ}む (work hard at job hunting)
- {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}が{終|お}わる (finish job hunting)
- {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}で{忙|いそが}しい (busy with job hunting)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese university students typically wear identical black "recruit suits" ({リクルートスーツ|りくるーとすーつ}) during {就職活動|しゅうしょくかつどう}. The uniformity is part of the expected etiquette.
